headline: High-risk filesystem and workflow orchestration pairing: n8n can read/write shared files and execute commands, while AutoGPT can also shell out and access the filesystem.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can read/write the filesystem and execute shell commands; B can write/read the server filesystem and orchestrate tools from workflow nodes. If B passes attacker-controlled file content into A, or A consumes B-produced files as instructions, prompt injection is plausible via the shared filesystem. No direct clipboard/MCP bridge is shown, so this is not high.
conditions: IF n8n writes untrusted workflow output into a file that AutoGPT later reads as instructions
IF AutoGPT ingests file contents from the shared server filesystem without provenance checks
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent's files
Prefix all handoff files with a strict schema and reject free-form text
Add a manual review step before AutoGPT reads n8n-generated files
Disable file-based handoffs for untrusted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to workflow artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly touches 'whatever the workflow processes' and has broad network egress plus server filesystem access; A also has filesystem access and allowlisted egress. If either agent processes sensitive workflow data, the other can read or transmit it through the shared server filesystem or outbound APIs. The profiles do not prove PHI or secrets, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF the workflow processes secrets, customer data, or regulated records
IF n8n stores those records on the shared server filesystem before AutoGPT can read them
mitigations: Restrict both agents to a dedicated non-sensitive workspace
Turn off file persistence for sensitive workflow steps
Mask secrets before writing workflow artifacts
Review outbound integrations used by n8n for data egress
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses; B can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the server filesystem. B also supports multiple instances with shared state via n8n datastore and connected systems, while A does not support multiple instances. Concurrent writes to the same filesystem or workflow artifacts can race and corrupt state; the default overlap is dangerous enough to rate high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or workflow artifact set
IF n8n runs multiple instances against shared datastore-backed state
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate writable directory
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue
Avoid concurrent execution of shell-writing steps
Keep n8n workflows single-writer for shared resources
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is an orchestration system that can call tools as workflow nodes, and A can generate outputs after shell/file operations. If B treats A's output as authoritative, it can trigger downstream actions such as API calls or command execution without verification. That creates a classic cascade from generated text to real actions, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF n8n feeds AutoGPT output directly into downstream workflow nodes
IF downstream nodes execute API calls or commands based on unverified A output
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before action nodes
Require structured outputs with validation rules
Compare A output against a second source before acting
Log and review all tool-triggering decisions
requires-engineering: add policy gates for high-impact workflow nodes

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles 'whatever the workflow processes' on a server filesystem with broad egress and per-integration OAuth/credential stores; A also has filesystem access and allowlisted egress. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a concrete compliance mismatch is unproven. Still, shared processing of regulated data could create retention or residency issues in default deployments.
conditions: IF the workflow processes regulated data such as EU PII, PHI, or secrets
IF n8n credentials or logs retain that data longer than the source system permits
mitigations: Confirm the data class before enabling the pair
Minimize retention in n8n execution logs
Store credentials only in the credential store, not workflow data
Route regulated data through a compliant isolated workspace
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
